cluster_name: Ratko Mladic dies in Hague detention serving genocide sentence
tldr: Headlines across 13 countries frame Mladic's death almost unanimously as a crime-and-punishment epitaph — labeling him 'war criminal,' 'Butcher of Bosnia,' or 'convicted of genocide' across at least 10 outlets. The Balkan regional press diverges sharply: Balkan Insight foregrounds Serbian President Vucic's political defiance of the UN court and a binary cultural split (war criminal or 'Serb hero'), while N1 focuses on the IRMCT's formal investigation into death circumstances. NPR World is the sole outlet to center a survivor voice in its headline, shifting frame from perpetrator identity to victim testimony. BBC Africa pivots entirely to a concurrent Rwanda genocide conviction in The Hague, treating international accountability for genocide as the systemic story rather than a Mladic obituary. La Jornada's headline contributes no encodable frame — its title is a generic column header — making Mexico the only bucket where the headline layer is editorially silent on the story.

silences.what_they_covered_instead: Russian state media — which would predictably adopt Vucic's framing of The Hague as an anti-Serb institution and contest the universal 'war criminal' label — is entirely absent from the headline layer; their counter-narrative is a structural gap in this corpus.

single_outlet_findings.finding: Pivots entirely to a concurrent Rwanda genocide conviction in The Hague rather than Mladic's death, implicitly treating both as instances of systemic international accountability for genocide rather than a Balkan-specific obituary.
Sole outlet to center a survivor's voice in its headline, foregrounding victim testimony over perpetrator identity — a framing absent from every other outlet in the cluster.

Title 'El Correo Ilustrado' is a generic reader-letters column header with no story framing; the headline layer contributes no encodable frame for this story despite the signal text covering Mladic's death.

Takes a retrospective accountability angle — where are the other key figures from the Balkan wars? — contextualizing Mladic's death within an incomplete accountability reckoning rather than treating it as a closed chapter.

bottom_line: The headline layer is overwhelmingly a crime-and-punishment epitaph — Mladic dies as 'war criminal' and 'Butcher of Bosnia' across 10 of 15 outlets and 10 of 13 countries — with a distinct Balkan counterthread foregrounding divided memory and Serbia's provocative state-honors burial plans diverging sharply from the international consensus.
